The main takeaway from our work is that
depth lower bounds against circuits can be obtained by restricting the orientation of gates, even when the weights of the gates are not too large.
the orientation of the functions computed by gates in a circuit can be a useful tool for proving lower bounds.
the orientation of a circuit is a natural measure of non-monatonicity, and it has the potential of capturing the complexity of functions that are beyond the scope of the monotone circuit model.
